reason: Section 84 is a large subdivision plan application source with separate topics for submitting the plan, plan content, and signatures/certification/street names.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision plan application, scale, material size, and approval space

evidenceText: written application for approval of a subdivision plan

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state who may apply, required copies, plan scales, material sizes, and space for approvals, assents, and filing particulars.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the application, copy, scale, material, and approval-space requirements for subdivision plans.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision plan title block, boundaries, streets, parcels, easements, monuments, and key plan

evidenceText: A subdivision plan shall set out the following

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections list the detailed information to be set out on the plan and require azimuths, distances, radii, central angles, and arcs for boundaries.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the major information and boundary data a subdivision plan must set out.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision plan preparation, owner signature, surveyor seal, proof, references, and street names

evidenceText: certified as correct and sealed by a New Brunswick Land Surveyor

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require the plan to be specially prepared, marked, signed, certified and sealed by a surveyor, accompanied by proof or authorization, allow references to filed plans, and govern street-name approval.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the signature, surveyor certification, supporting documents, filed-plan references, and street-name approval requirements for subdivision plans.

reason: Section 85 is a focused approval and filing effect rule for subdivision plans.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision plan approval stamp, registrar filing, approved area, and copy return

evidenceText: shall be signified on the face of the plan

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections describe how approval is shown, registrar filing without proof, the limited area approved, when filing makes the plan valid, and return of copies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how subdivision plan approval is signified, filed, limited to marked boundaries, and returned after approval.

reason: Section 86 is a coherent filing workflow for approved subdivision plans and post-filing copies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision plan filing, one-year approval period, registrar endorsement, and official-use copies

evidenceText: no subdivision plan in respect of which a subdivision by-law or regulation is in effect may be filed

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require development officer approval before filing, limit approval to one year unless filed, require deposit of approved copies, direct registrar endorsement and distribution, and restrict development officer copy use.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the filing prerequisites, approval expiry, registrar duties, copy distribution, and official-use marking for subdivision plans.

reason: Section 87 is a large road-and-street subdivision source with distinct assent triggers, infrastructure prerequisites, and vesting effects.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister assent required for public or future streets in listed subdivisions

evidenceText: approval of the plan by the development officer shall not be given until

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify when Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure assent is required before development officer approval of subdivision plans laying out public or future streets.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when subdivision plans with public or future streets need Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure assent.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Water, sewer, street construction, bonds, certification, and endorsed assent

evidenceText: The assent of the Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure under this section shall not be given until

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state prerequisites for Ministerial assent, including recommendations, water or sewer agreements and guarantees, street construction or bonds, certification, binding agreements, and signature endorsement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the infrastructure, bond, agreement, certification, and endorsement requirements before Ministerial assent is given.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown vesting of streets, easements, and water or sewer systems on subdivision filing
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern notation of separate assent documents, vesting of public and future streets, vesting of easement rights, public utility meaning, and vesting and filing of certified water or sewer systems.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what vests in the Crown or public utilities when assented subdivision plans and related documents are filed.

reason: Section 88 is a large local-government assent source with separate assent triggers, recommendation/certification requirements, and vesting effects.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Council or rural community assent for streets and public-purpose land

evidenceText: approval of the plan by the development officer shall not be given until

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify when municipal or rural community council assent is required before approval for plans laying out public or future streets or setting aside public-purpose land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council or rural community assent is required for subdivision plans involving streets or public-purpose land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recommendations, corporate certification, and street-location considerations for assent
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state recommendation and facilities prerequisites, how assent is certified and endorsed, and the topography, lot, intersection, access, and future-subdivision considerations for street recommendations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what must happen before local-government assent and what factors guide street-location recommendations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local government vesting of streets, public-purpose land, and easements on filing

evidenceText: free from any lien or encumbrance

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state how public streets, future streets, land for public purposes, and easement rights vest on filing an assented and approved plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what vests in the local government or public utility when an assented subdivision plan is filed.

reason: Section 89 separates amending subdivision plan procedure from vesting effects and new-use transfer requirements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Amending subdivision plan form, approvals, filing, and registrar endorsement

evidenceText: may be amended by a new subdivision plan

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections describe an amending subdivision plan, its approval and filing treatment, required registration data, and registrar endorsement on the amended plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a filed subdivision plan may be amended and how the registrar records the amendment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Vesting of streets or public-purpose land under amending subdivision plans

evidenceText: On the filing of an amending subdivision plan

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 89(3) states how land indicated as streets or public-purpose land vests in the Crown or local government when an amending plan is filed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how streets and public-purpose land vest when an amending subdivision plan is filed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: New uses, discontinued streets, transfer documents, and new-owner vesting

evidenceText: the new use of the land shall be indicated

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address land previously vested for streets or public purposes that will be used differently, including required indications, highway-discontinuance certificate, transfer documents, and vesting in the new owner.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what is required when an amending subdivision plan changes the use of previously vested street or public-purpose land.

reason: Section 90 is a coherent alternate plan process for local government acquisition that would otherwise subdivide land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local government acquisition plans that subdivide land

evidenceText: If a purchase or other acquisition of land by a local government

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow council to prepare and file a certified plan instead of complying with other subdivision provisions and require references and registrar endorsements if filed plans are altered.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the alternate plan process when local government land acquisition would subdivide land and how altered filed plans are endorsed.

reason: Section 91 separates development charge by-law authority and preparation from eligible capital costs and special-account use.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development charge by-law authority, agreements, preparation, and certification

evidenceText: provides for the imposition and payment of a development charge

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize development charge by-laws and agreements and set direction, consultation, and certification requirements for making or amending them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a development charge by-law may impose or authorize and how it must be prepared and certified.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Eligible capital costs and single collection of development charges

evidenceText: may be used only to pay for all or part of the on or off-site capital cost

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections limit development charges to listed on-site or off-site capital costs and allow collection once for an authorized purpose specified in the agreement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the capital costs that development charges may fund and when a charge may be collected once for a purpose.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special account and purpose-limited spending for development charges
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 91(4) requires development charge money to be paid into a special account and spent only for the specific purpose for which it was collected.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how development charge money must be held and spent.

reason: Section 92 is a focused rule for development charge agreements and by-law-prescribed agreement circumstances.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development charge agreement payments, services in lieu, security, and by-law terms

evidenceText: may enter into a development charge agreement

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections state what a development charge agreement may provide and allow the by-law to prescribe when such agreements are used and their general terms.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a development charge agreement may cover and what a development charge by-law may prescribe about those agreements.

reason: Section 93 provides substantive validity and commencement conditions for a development charge by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development charge by-law validity and filing commencement

evidenceText: No development charge by-law is valid unless

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify certification, section 111 compliance, paragraph 112(1)(b) compliance, and commencement on filing or a later by-law date.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the validity requirements for a development charge by-law and when it comes into force.
